title: AI Use Case Spotting and Automation Discovery

questions.question: What must a discovery conversation expose before an AI idea can be treated as a use case?
options: The workflow, observable pain, available data, owner, risk, and a value measure
A preferred vendor and a promise that the model will replace the whole workflow
A polished demo, even if nobody can name the decision or the affected metric
A long list of possible prompts without a person responsible for the outcome
questions.explanation: The canvas turns enthusiasm into a testable plan by naming the workflow, signals, owner, risk, and metric. A tool choice or prompt list does not establish that the work is viable.

questions.question: For Scenario("manual reporting", ..., ("repeatable workflow", "text-heavy input"), impact=4, uncertainty=3, what score does score_scenario return?
options: 11, because only impact and uncertainty contribute
15, from 4 times 2 plus 3 plus two matched signals at two points each
17, because every control adds two points to the scenario
20, because any scenario with text-heavy input is capped immediately
questions.explanation: The base is 4 times 2 plus 3, or 11. The two matched signals add 4, giving 15, below the cap of 20.

questions.question: Which rule does score_scenario apply after counting matched signals?
options: It divides the impact by the number of signals to avoid rewarding busy workflows
It returns the raw score even when a scenario has more than twenty points
It adds two points per match to impact times two plus uncertainty, then caps the result at 20
It assigns launch gate required whenever the description contains the word owner
questions.explanation: The implementation computes base = impact * 2 + uncertainty, adds len(matches) * 2, and wraps the result in min(20, ...). Priority is decided separately.

questions.question: A scenario contains three recognized signals. Which controls does recommend select with the lesson's CONTROLS list?
options: Only owner signoff, because the final control is the most important one
No controls until the score reaches the launch-gate threshold
The first two controls only, regardless of how many signals matched
The first four controls: pilot metric, risk review, data readiness check, and owner signoff
questions.explanation: recommend slices CONTROLS to 1 plus the match count, with a minimum of two and a maximum of the full list. Three matches therefore select all four controls.

questions.question: What category does choose_category return for a Scenario with no matched signals?
options: assist, the first entry in CATEGORIES
predict, because missing signals imply a forecasting problem
automate, because an empty signal list is treated as a fast path
retrieve, because discovery starts with searching for more data
questions.explanation: The no-match branch returns CATEGORIES[0]. In this lesson that list begins with assist; it does not guess a more specific solution from missing evidence.

questions.question: Why does build_plan sort its rows by score before printing the reusable discovery canvas?
options: It hides low-scoring ideas so the workshop only discusses the top row
It lets a team review the highest-scoring scenarios first while retaining category, priority, controls, and rationale for each row
It changes every scenario's score to its position in the portfolio
It converts each Scenario into a final deployment ticket without a human decision
questions.explanation: build_plan keeps one output row per scenario, then sorts by score in descending order. The ordering supports prioritization; the returned fields still show why each row received its score.
